subject: strange results with lincombs in bym2 model

messages.author: f1572a038d61492c
messages.subject: strange results with lincombs in bym2 model
parts:
Hi,

I noticed some strange results when using lincombs and a bym2 spatial model. I have attached a script, an .rda file and an adjacency matrix here.

I am fitting the following model:

logit.est ~ 1 + f(area.struct, model = "bym2", graph = admin2.mat, 
    constr = T, hyper = list(phi = list(prior = "pc", param = c(0.5, 
        0.5)), prec = list(prior = "pc.prec", param = c(u0/4, 
        0.01))), scale.model = T)

and this is my inla call, note logit.prec are fixed precisions.

n.likelihood <- 1
mod <- inla(formula.inla, family = rep("gaussian", n.likelihood),
            data = data.inla,
            control.fixed = list(prec.intercept = 1), 
            control.family = list(hyper= list(prec = list(initial= log(1),
                                                          fixed= TRUE ))),
            control.predictor = list(compute = T, link = 1),
            control.inla = list(int.strategy = 'eb'),
            scale = data.model$logit.prec, 
            lincomb = lincombs,
            verbose = T)

It's worth noting that fitting this model is exploratory, and the data we use does have replicates, but I am still curious about the strane behavior I've found. I was modifying old code so I just defined lincombs for each of my areas, but the linear combination is the same as the linear predictor, i.e. it has the fixed intercept and the bym2 term for the area of interest. However, the results are different when i look at mod$summary.lincomb.derived and mod$summary.linear.predctor. Moreover, the sds for the lincombs are zero. Does anyone know what would lead to this behavior? This does not happen if I specify f() as 'iid' instead of the bym2.

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] strange results with lincombs in bym2 model
parts:
I think the issue is that you have a double index in the definition,
like here:

> str(lincombs[[1]])
List of 3
$ :List of 1
..$ (Intercept):List of 1
.. ..$ weight: num 1
$ :List of 1
..$ area.struct:List of 2
.. ..$ idx : int 1
.. ..$ weight: num 1
$ :List of 1
..$ area.struct:List of 2
.. ..$ idx : int 1
.. ..$ weight: num 1


you see that 'area.struct' have idx=1 twice. you see this also in the
log, as

Number of non-zero weights [3]
Lincomb = idx weight
28 1.0000000000
28 1.0000000000
84 1.0000000000


'28' appears twice.

you see this for others as well.

this is what cause the problem.

H
